guardian.description:
Eighteen children among the people killed after ferry capsized on Lake Kariba

Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe, taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.

The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba, on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it turned over during heavy winds.

lemonde.title: « Notre voisine hurlait : “Les talibans reviennent !”, nous étions pétrifiées » : cinq ans après le 15 août 2021, des Afghanes racontent leur enfer
lemonde.description: « Paroles d’Afghanes » (1/6). Cinq ans après le retour des talibans au pouvoir avec leur charia archaïque, notre envoyée spéciale à Kaboul a fait témoigner ces femmes presque invisibles sur la peur au quotidien, le joug de la famille, les mariages forcés et leurs rêves confisqués.

lemonde.title: Léon Marchand champion d’Europe sur 400 m nage libre : la réinvention du nageur français, qu’on n’attendait pas sur cette distance
lemonde.description: Le quadruple champion olympique français a décroché son deuxième titre continental en deux jours, dimanche, en remportant cette fois la finale du 400 m nage libre. De très bon augure dans la perspective des Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028.

lemonde.title: Avec la canicule, les équarrisseurs croulent sous les cadavres de volailles en décomposition dont l’odeur exaspère riverains et pouvoirs publics
lemonde.description: La surmortalité dans les élevages lors de la vague de chaleur de la fin juin a provoqué un embouteillage des usines chargées de leur traitement, créant des nuisances olfactives qui ont fini par exaspérer les habitants.

lemonde.title: Le RC Lens remporte le premier Trophée des champions de son histoire face au PSG
lemonde.description: Longtemps réduit à dix, les Sang et Or l’ont emporté contre le PSG (1-0), dimanche, à Lens. Trois mois après la Coupe de France, ils glanent un nouveau titre et privent les Parisiens d’un deuxième trophée après leur succès en Supercoupe d’Europe, mercredi 12 août.

lemonde.title: « L’extrême droite française a voué une détestation tenace au général de Gaulle ; aujourd’hui, elle pourrait réussir sa stratégie de captation d’héritage »
lemonde.description: A huit mois de l’élection présidentielle, et alors que de Gaulle est plébiscité au cinéma, le documentariste Jonathan Hayoun observe, dans une tribune au « Monde », que la mémoire du Général est devenue un héritage à prendre, et qu’il s’agirait de ne pas laisser l’extrême droite s’en emparer pour réécrire son histoire.

lemonde.title: De plus amples dérives éthiques identifiées dans des publications scientifiques de l’IHU de Marseille

lemonde.description: Le jeune français de 19 ans a remporté, dimanche, le Grand Smash d’Europe à Malmö. Il devient le premier pongiste tricolore de l’histoire à s’imposer en individuel lors d’un tournoi de ce niveau, équivalent d’un Grand Chelem en tennis.

lemonde.title: Vidéo : quatre semaines à bord d’un brise-glace, ces navires à la technologie de plus en plus convoitée
lemonde.description: « Terre de glace » (1/4). Capables de traverser des zones maritimes entièrement glacées, ces navires sont devenus stratégiques, dans un contexte de conflit d’influences entre puissances dans l’Arctique. Notre journaliste, Léa Bello, embarque tout le mois d’août sur l’un d’eux à l’occasion d’une expédition scientifique exceptionnelle.

lemonde.title: Entre enquête familiale et journal intime, la fille d’Igor Bogdanoff entreprend le deuil de son père
lemonde.description: Depuis la mort des médiatiques jumeaux, il y a quatre ans, Anna Ostasenko Bogdanoff  était hantée par son lourd héritage familial. La documentariste et vidéaste de 35 ans en explore les méandres et exorcise ses névroses dans un premier roman, « Rappelle-moi, ma belle », en librairie le 19 août.

lemonde.title: En Sierra Leone, la cohabitation exemplaire des chrétiens et des musulmans, loin des tensions confessionnelles des pays de la région
lemonde.description: Contrairement au Mali, au Niger, au Burkina Faso ou au Nigeria, minés par les divisions religieuses, l’ancienne colonie britannique voit sa population vivre sereinement sa foi. Chaque famille ou presque est interconfessionnelle, et les leaders religieux n’ont de cesse de promouvoir la cohésion nationale.

lemonde.title: Gaza : Huit pays musulmans condamnent le « refus israélien » de poursuivre le plan de Donald Trump pour mettre fin de la guerre

rfi.title: Belgium turns to European air support as wildfire rages near German border

rfi.title: Europe's shrinking rivers give rise to debate over how to tackle drought
rfi.description: Europe's shrinking rivers are disrupting industry, reducing power generation and intensifying the debate over how to respond to worsening drought. As water levels fall across the continent, authorities and businesses alike are looking for ways to keep freight moving and critical infrastructure operating. Hydrologists warn, however, that digging rivers deeper cannot create more water and could make shortages worse.

rfi.title: Solar-powered community gardens offer lifeline in drought-hit Zimbabwe
rfi.description: At a shared garden in eastern Zimbabwe, solar-powered pumps are helping farmers grow crops year round, even when drought dries out other fields.

rfi.title: Obesity rises sharply as French Polynesia faces chronic health challenges
rfi.description: French Polynesia is facing growing public health pressures as rising rates of chronic disease combine with an ageing population and changing lifestyles. More than half of adult residents are now considered obese.

rfi.title: Morocco arrests nearly 300 migrants near Ceuta amid renewed crossing fears
rfi.description: Scores of would-be migrants, most of them from sub-Saharan Africa, were intercepted in northern Morocco near the border with the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Saturday, two weeks after tens of thousands of people attempted to enter the territory.

rfi.title: France probes unprecedented cyberattack after tax data of 678,000 users stolen
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a major cyberattack on the country’s tax administration that affected nearly 700,000 individuals and businesses, authorities said on Saturday.

rfi.title: France's successive heatwaves show strain of living in urban 'heat islands'
rfi.description: As France experiences its latest heatwave, residents of urban "heat islands" – dense neighbourhoods with few trees or green spaces – are suffering acutely in the high temperatures, and local authorities are searching for solutions.

rfi.title: Algeria edge Morocco on penalties in WAFCON third-place play-off
rfi.description: Morocco endured a second painful penalty shootout defeat in the space of four days as Algeria claimed third place at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations on Saturday following a 1-1 draw in Rabat.

rfi.title: Armenian Genocide survivors' grandson says 'political motives' block recognition
rfi.description: In 1915, the Ottoman Empire began the systematic deportation and massacre of its Armenian population. As many as 1.5 million Armenians were killed – widely regarded by historians as the twentieth century's first genocide, and the event for which the term was later coined. Stephan Pechdimaldji, the grandson of two of the survivors, spoke to RFI about why recognition still matters.

rfi.title: Nine killed in Israeli strikes on Lebanon as tensions test peace framework
rfi.description: At least nine people were killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon on Saturday, according to Lebanon’s state news agency, in some of the deadliest attacks since Beirut agreed to a US-mediated framework aimed at ending the latest round of fighting.

rfi.title: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghanistan seeks to ease international isolation
rfi.description: In the five years since the Taliban seized back power in Afghanistan, the country's worsening human rights record has drawn sanctions and aid cuts. But despite refusing to officially recognise the fundamentalist movement's government, some countries are concluding that engaging with the Taliban has become unavoidable.

rfi.title: In Turkey, one of the world's longest conflicts reaches a turning point
rfi.description: Turkey stands on the threshold of closing a conflict spanning almost 50 years, after the Turkish parliament this week passed a law allowing exiled Kurdish militants to return home and rejoin society. The legislation aims to end the war with the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which has battled the Turkish state for independence since 1984.

rfi.title: Law on assisted dying wins constitutional approval in France
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council on Friday approved a law creating a right to assisted dying, removing the last major legal obstacle before the measure can be enacted and implemented.

rfi.title: Fake accounts and false rumours drive new Ceuta crossing campaign
rfi.description: Calls for a new mass crossing into Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on Morocco's Mediterranean coast, have flooded Moroccan social media, with posts urging migrants to rush the border on Saturday. An RFI investigation found the campaign was fuelled by false rumours, suspicious accounts and signs of artificial amplification.

rfi.title: US missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after more than nine months
rfi.description: American Kevin Rideout, who worked as a pilot for an evangelical organisation, has been freed after he was kidnapped in October 2025 in Niamey. His release comes as the security situation remains tense in Niger.

rfi.title: Top French court scraps social media ban for children under 15
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council struck down a law on Friday that would have banned children under 15 from using social media from September. The judges ruled that the measure placed a disproportionate restriction on freedom of expression and communication.

rfi.title: French firefighters threaten to strike over lack of resources
rfi.description: As wildfires continue to burn across France, representatives of firefighters' unions said they would go on strike in September to protest a lack of resources. Despite a meeting with the interior minister on Thursday, they say they are unhappy with the government's response so far.

zeit.title: Reform des Unterhaltsvorschusses: SPD lehnt Kürzung von Unterhaltsvorschuss für Jugendliche ab
zeit.description: Die SPD ist dagegen, den staatlichen Unterhaltsvorschuss nur noch bis zum 16. Lebensjahr zu zahlen. Stattdessen will sie die Regeln für Unterhaltspflichtige verschärfen.

Waldbrand: Brand im Hohen Venn: Evakuierung bei Monschau angeordnet

Leichtathletik-EM: Hindernisläufer Ruppert gewinnt EM-Gold
zeit.description: Das deutsche Team hat bei der Leichtathletik-EM zwei weitere Medaillen gewonnen. Frederik Ruppert hat über 3.000 Meter Hindernis Gold geholt und Karl Bebendorf Bronze.

zeit.title: BSW-Gründerin : Wagenknecht ruft Höcke erneut zu Gespräch über Thüringer Regierung auf
zeit.description: Sahra Wagenknecht fordert einen neuen Ministerpräsidenten in Thüringen. Sie appelliert an Björn Höcke, öffentlich über einen überparteilichen Kandidaten zu debattieren.

zeit.title: Waldbrände in NRW und Belgien: Hürtgenwald-Brand unter Kontrolle – Belgien fordert deutsche Hilfe an
zeit.description: Tagelange haben Einsatzkräfte die Großfeuer im Hürtgenwald und Hohen Venn bekämpft. Die Großbrände scheinen eingedämmt. Belgien setzt auf Hilfe deutscher Einsatzkräfte.

zeit.title: General Jared Sembritzki: Die Deutschen sollen der Amboss sein
zeit.description: Jared Sembritzki ist wohl der kriegerischste General Deutschlands. Er kommandiert 18.000 Soldaten und bereitet sie auf alles vor, was möglich wäre.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Wegen Waldbrand – die Stadt Monschau in Nordrhein-Westfalen wird in Teilen evakuiert
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: Dominic Lobalu läuft über 10 000 m ebenso auf den zweiten Platz wie die 4-mal-100-m-Staffel der Frauen
nzz.description: Für das Staffelteam ist es die erste Medaille – mehr als zehn Jahre wartete es auf diesen Moment. Die Schweiz steht nun bei sieben Medaillen.

nzz.title: Vorbild Pierre Maudet: Valérie Dittli kandidiert erneut für die Waadtländer Regierung – notfalls wohl ohne ihre Mitte-Partei
nzz.description: Das Präsidium der Kantonalpartei will die umstrittene Staatsrätin loswerden. Doch Dittli setzt auf die Parteibasis. Und einen früheren FDP-Mann.

nzz.title: Der Schwägalp-Schwinget steht ganz im Zeichen des Duells der Ostschweiz gegen Bern – am Ende triumphieren die Gäste mit Fabian Staudenmann
nzz.description: Der Fuss des Säntis ist am Ende in Berner Hand. Die Gastgeber haben beim letzten Bergfest der Saison das Nachsehen – bester Einheimischer wird der Schwingerkönig Armon Orlik auf Rang 4.

nzz.title: Mindestens 80 Tote bei Bootsunglück in Simbabwe
nzz.description: Eine überfüllte Fähre kentert auf dem Karibasee in Simbabwe. Mindestens 80 Menschen sterben. Noch immer werden Leichen geborgen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: SVP-Nationalrat Lukas Reimann wird in die Wiler Stadt-Exekutive gewählt +++ Italienische Bergführer setzen Matterhorn-Touren aus
Wie ein Dorf im Westjordanland zum Symbol für Israels Passivität gegenüber radikalen Siedlern wurde
nzz.description: Seit sechs Tagen wird der palästinensische Ort Kusra belagert. Doch Jerusalem hält sich auffällig zurück, trotz wachsendem Druck aus dem Ausland.

nzz.title: Grönland stoppt Bohrpläne eines Trump-nahen Erdölkonsortiums
nzz.description: Die USA haben ihre Drohungen mit einer militärischen Besetzung der arktischen Insel zwar vorerst aufgegeben. Aber sie wollen weitere Stützpunkte errichten. Zudem sorgen forsche amerikanische Investoren mit Rohstoffprojekten für Spannungen.

nzz.title: 73-Jährige stirbt bei Unfall im Engadin: Polizei spricht vom schwersten Kutschenunglück der letzten Jahre in Graubünden
nzz.description: Bei einem Unfall mit einer Kutschenkomposition im Val Roseg kam am Samstag eine Frau ums Leben. Zwölf weitere Personen wurden verletzt.

nzz.title: Der Gedanke an seine Familie gibt ihm Energie – Amanal Petros gewinnt Marathon-Gold an den Leichtathletik-EM
nzz.description: Ein Jahr nach seiner knappen WM-Niederlage holte der Deutsche in Birmingham Gold. Im Moment des Triumphs dachte er wie immer an seine Familie, die noch immer in der Konfliktregion Tigray lebt.

nzz.title: Am Zuricrit im Kreis 4 fährt sogar die Tour-de-France-Siegerin mit – das weckt Erinnerungen an die wilden Zürcher Sechstagerennen
nzz.description: Am Quartierrennen Zuricrit zelebriert der Radsport seine vorbildliche Volksnähe. Für Furore sorgen Demi Vollering und Mauro Schmid, die schon an der Tour de France brillierten. Ein Augenschein im Lochergut.

nzz.title: «Trete an, um zu gewinnen»: Valérie Dittli will trotz Widerstand der eigenen Partei erneut antreten
nzz.description: Die Waadtländer Staatsrätin gibt in einem Zeitungsinterview ihre Kandidatur bekannt.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Migrantenansturm in Ceuta: Marokko nimmt Migranten vor Ceuta fest +++ Spanien führt Grenzkontrollen für Reisende aus Italien ein
nzz.description: Die Lage in der spanischen Exklave Ceuta in Nordafrika ist nach der Ankunft Tausender Migranten angespannt. Die neusten Meldungen zur Migrationskrise.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Erdbeben in Kolumbien: Zahl der Toten steigt auf rund 290
nzz.description: Ein starkes Erdbeben hat am Montag Kolumbien erschüttert. Zahlreiche Gebäude stürzten ein und die Zahl der Verletzten könnte sich auf mehrere Hunderte belaufen. Die wichtigsten Antworten.

nzz.title: Ceuta bleibt dicht, doch die Krise ist nicht vorbei
nzz.description: Trotz Aufrufen zum illegalen Grenzübertritt ist ein erneuter Ansturm auf die spanische Exklave am Wochenende ausgeblieben. Aber die Lage der in Ceuta nur notdürftig untergebrachten Migranten ist weiterhin ernst.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Libanon meldet Tote Angriffen im Süden des Landes​​​ +++ Trump will Strasse von Hormuz zu US-Territorium machen
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

observador.title: Todos, todos, todos
observador.description: A ortodoxia católica aceita, mas diz: nós aceitamos-te e acolhemos-te exatamente como és, mas amamos-te demais para te deixar assim.

observador.title: A poupança dos particulares não pode continuar a pagar 28%
observador.description: Existe uma contradição difícil de ignorar entre o incentivo à poupança e a tributação aplicada aos particulares que efetivamente conseguem poupar.

observador.title: O monte que ninguém decidiu desfazer
observador.description: A revisão do mercado europeu de carbono não abandona a meta climática de 2040. Subtrai-lhe ambição um grão de cada vez, e é essa aritmética discreta, não a rutura anunciada, que devíamos temer.

observador.title: #PéAntePé
observador.description: Talvez os pés sejam o currículo silencioso do corpo. Dizem se caminhámos, se corremos, se dançámos ou se passámos a vida sentados à espera do que fortuitamente acontecia.

observador.title: A democracia também se constrói fora da política
observador.description: As fundações podem ser uma espécie de capital paciente da democracia.

observador.title: O Nosso Maior Legado
observador.description: Os portugueses têm razões para ser o povo mais orgulhoso do mundo na sua língua. Nenhum outro país multiplicou de forma tão expressiva o número de falantes do seu idioma.

observador.title: O conhecimento também salva vidas
observador.description: Talvez tenha chegado o momento de deixarmos de avaliar os bombeiros apenas  pela forma como respondem às ocorrências e começarmos também a avaliá-los  pela forma como aprendem com elas.

observador.title: A Europa e o dilema do futuro do futebol mundial
observador.description: A UEFA possui inegavelmente o peso específico para tomar nas nossas mãos o futuro da modalidade.

observador.title: As crianças que não veem morrer
observador.description: Talvez tenhamos confundido proteger com esconder. Porque não podemos proteger os nossos filhos da morte para sempre.

observador.title: Trocou a rede de carga para carros EV, pelos carros voadores
observador.description: Não vai ser possível democratizar os veículos eléctricos, sem que os países e as cidades criarem uma rede de postos de carga eficaz e numerosa. Mas há quem tenha trocado esta rede por carros voadores.

observador.title: Venezuela. Bispo do Funchal faz visita às vítimas do sismo
observador.description: Bispo do Funchal fez visita seis dias à Venezuela. Nuno Brás da Silva pediu ajuda e solidariedade para com as vítimas do sismo onde morreram mais de seis mil pessoas.

observador.title: As notícias das 23h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Fogo em Torre de Moncorvo alastrou para Carrazeda de Ansiães
observador.description: Incêndio em Torre de Moncorvo alastrou para o município vizinho de Carrazeda de Ansiães e tem duas frentes ativas. Mais de 300 bombeiros combatem as chamas.

observador.title: Com "PM desligado da realidade", Carneiro persegue Guterres
observador.description: No Algarve, há 31 anos, Guterres deu o pontapé de saída para uma maioria socialista. Agora, José Luís Carneiro traz momento à memória e faz contas a dez anos. Montenegro foi alvo a abater.

observador.title: Marítimo soma segunda vitória no campeonato
observador.description: Marítimo derrotou o Famalicão com um golo aos 90+4, assinado por Maurice Boakye. Equipa iguala FC Porto e Arouca na liderança.

observador.title: Alpine voltará ao A110 a gasolina a pedido de um “amigo”?
observador.description: A Alpine fez saber que 2026 marcará o fim do A110 a combustão, para dar origem ao A110 eléctrico em 2027. Mas, segundo o CEO, é provável que um mercado (onde nunca vendeu) queira um A110 a gasolina.

observador.title: Ações na Microsoft de 1,5 milhões e um corte anual de 90 mil
observador.description: Pedro Duarte auferiu 192 mil euros no último ano completo no privado. Entrou para o Parlamento antes de ter um contrato de trabalho e recebeu salário em stock awards enquanto dirigente da Microsoft.

observador.title: Lens vence PSG e conquista Supertaça Francesa
observador.description: Um golo de Florian Thauvin aos 32' foi o suficiente para fechar a história de um marcador que sorriu aos 'underdogs' (1-0). O Lens jogou com menos uma unidade durante cerca de uma hora de partida.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump va réduire "considérablement" les exercices militaires conjoints avec la Corée du Sud
france24fr.description: Le président américain a déclaré, dimanche via son réseau Truth Social, avoir demandé de réduire de manière significative les exercices militaires conjoints avec la Corée du Sud devant débuter lundi. Des exercices "coûteux" qui "envoient un signal totalement inapproprié et hostile" envers Pyongyang, selon Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Le ministre de la communication tchadien nous répond sur France 24
france24fr.description: Se dirige t-on vers un apaisement du climat politique au Tchad ? Une question légitime après la grâce accordée vendredi à 9 opposants par le président Déby. Le ministre de la communication tchadien Gassim Chérif est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Football : le Racing ⁠Club de ​Lens remporte le Trophée des champions face au PSG
france24fr.description: Le Racing ⁠Club de ​Lens, pourtant réduit à dix, s'est offert dimanche son premier Trophée des champions en battant le Paris Saint-Germain (1 à 0). Vainqueurs ‌de la Coupe de France, les hommes ⁠de Dino Toppmöller ont ouvert le score à la ‌32e minute par l'intermédiaire de leur capitaine.

france24fr.title: Athlétisme : le perchiste Armand Duplantis à nouveau champion d’Europe, Baptiste Thiery en bronze
france24fr.description: Double champion olympique, Armand Duplantis a remporté son quatrième titre consécutif de champion d’Europe dimanche soir à Birmingham. Le perchiste suédois a assuré le titre en étant le seul à franchir 6,15 m, devançant le Grec Emmanouil Karalis (6,00 m) et le Français Baptiste Thiery (5,85 m).

france24fr.title: 🔴 CAN 2026 féminine : le Cameroun remporte la finale contre le Malawi
CAN 2026 féminine : le Cameroun décroche le titre pour la première fois de son histoire
france24fr.description: Les Camerounaises ont gagné dimanche la finale de la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations féminine, à Rabat, au Maroc, en renversant le Malawi (3-0). Bien que plusieurs fois placées, les Lionnes indomptables camerounaises n'ont jamais été sacrées.

france24fr.title: Le pongiste Félix Lebrun remporte son premier Grand Smash, l'équivalent d'un Grand Chelem
Tennis de table : Félix Lebrun remporte son premier Grand Smash
france24fr.description: Le pongiste français Félix Lebrun a remporté dimanche un Grand Smash, l'équivalent d'un Grand Chelem en tennis, à Malmö en Suède. Une première pour le tennis de table français.

france24fr.title: Léon Marchand, champion d’Europe sur 400 mètres nage libre, nouvelle médaille d'or pour la France
Léon Marchand, champion d’Europe sur 400 m nage libre, nouvelle médaille d'or pour la France
france24fr.description: Le nageur français Léon Marchand a remporté dimanche la finale du 400 mètres nage libre lors des championnats d'Europe de natation à Saint-Denis, près de Paris. Il bat le record de France en 3 min 43 sec 14 et apporte une nouvelle médaille d'or à l'équipe de France.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : les régates de pirogues, une tradition vieille de deux siècles à Saint-Louis
france24fr.description: À Saint-Louis, au Sénégal, les traditionnelles régates de pirogues perpétuent une tradition vieille de près de deux siècles. Dans le quartier de pêcheurs de Guet Ndar, cette course de 3,5 km rassemble chaque année rameurs et habitants autour d'un événement culturel et sportif majeur. Mais malgré son succès populaire et les revenus qu'elle génère, les participants ne sont pas rémunérés et réclament davantage de reconnaissance pour cette discipline.

france24fr.title: Tchad : l'opposant Succès Masra s’exprime après sa libération
france24fr.description: L’opposant tchadien et ancien Premier ministre Succès Masra, fondateur du parti Les Transformateurs et candidat face au président Mahamat Idriss Déby à la présidentielle de 2024, avait été condamné à 20 ans de prison en 2025. Gracié par le président Déby le 14 août après plus d’un an derrière les barreaux, il s’est confié à FRANCE 24 sur la situation politique au Tchad et sur son avenir politique.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : un protocole pour démobiliser les rebelles rwandais des FDLR
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, les États-Unis disent avoir pris bonne note du protocole de démobilisation des FDLR, un groupe rebelle rwandais, présenté par Kinshasa fin juillet. Pour le gouvernement congolais, ce protocole constitue une première traduction concrète des engagements pris dans le cadre de l'accord de paix signé à Washington.

france24fr.title: Kenya : un mal mystérieux décime les éléphants
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, un mystérieux mal décime les éléphants dans une région touristique du sud du pays. Au moins 20 pachydermes sont morts depuis juin. Les autorités évoquent des traces de cyanure, une piste qui laisse sceptiques agriculteurs et scientifiques.

france24fr.title: L'Iran promet une prime de 30 000 dollars pour la mort ou la capture de soldats américains
france24fr.description: La République islamique d'Iran a annoncé dimanche une prime à quiconque tuerait ou capturerait un soldat américain. Le montant minimum s'élève à 30 000 dollars et sera doublé si une femme réalise l'action.

france24fr.title: Zimbabwe : le bilan monte à 84 morts dans le naufrage d'un ferry sur le lac Kariba
france24fr.description: Un ferry de passagers surchargé a chaviré mardi sur le lac Kariba, au Zimbabwe. Le bilan a été revu à la hausse dimanche après la découverte de nouveaux corps, portant à 84 le nombre de personnes noyées, selon la police.

france24fr.title: Sport féminin : les athlètes encore loin de l'égalité !
france24fr.description: La finale de la CAN féminine 2026, qui oppose le Cameroun au Malawi, est l'occasion de s'intéresser plus largement à la place des femmes dans le sport. Malgré une visibilité et un nombre de fans en hausse, les sportives restent confrontées à des conditions d'exercice moins favorables que leurs homologues masculins, à un manque de médiatisation et de financement, ainsi qu'à des problèmes persistants comme les agressions sexuelles. france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : Moscou visée par 600 drones, Kiev par des missiles balistiques
france24fr.description: Moscou a été visée par 600 drones la nuit de samedi à dimanche, une attaque d'une rare ampleur, tandis que Kiev était la même nuit attaquée aux missiles balistiques, chaque capitale enregistrant trois blessés.

spiegel.title: Monschau: 17 Häuser wegen Waldbrand im Hohen Venn evakuiert
spiegel.description: Der Großbrand in Belgien bedroht auch das deutsche Grenzgebiet. In Monschau werden 17 Häuser evakuiert. Hunderte Einsatzkräfte kämpfen gegen die Flammen. Doch der starke Wind erschwert die Löscharbeiten.

spiegel.title: Jason Arday: Zehntausende fordern Untersuchung nach Tod des Cambridge-Professors
spiegel.description: Nach dem Tod des 41-jährigen Soziologen Jason Arday wächst in Großbritannien der Druck auf die Regierung: Mehr als 31.000 Menschen fordern Aufklärung nach einer mutmaßlich rassistischen Kampagne gegen ihn.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM in Birmingham: Malaika Mihambo verpasst Medaille im Weitsprung
spiegel.description: Bei einem wahren Zielspringen an die Sieben-Meter-Marke blieb Favoritin Malaika Mihambo überraschend ohne EM-Medaille. Das ging ihr merklich nahe, wie ein bewegendes Interview zeigte.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Julia Ulbricht gewinnt sensationell Silber im Speerwurf
spiegel.description: Julia Ulbricht hat völlig überraschend die erste EM-Medaille der deutschen Speerwerferinnen seit acht Jahren gewonnen. Die Deutsche Meisterin erfüllte sich einen Traum – und nahm direkt den nächsten ins Visier.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Frederik Ruppert läuft zu Gold über 3000 Meter Hindernis
spiegel.description: Frederik Ruppert war über die 3000 Meter Hindernis als Favorit angetreten, komplett souverän gewann er EM-Gold. Mit einem starken Schlussspurt folgte Karl Bebendorf seinem Teamkollegen aufs Podest.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM in Birmingham: Deutsche 4x100-Mixed-Staffel holt Silber
spiegel.description: Bei der EM-Premiere über 4x100 Meter war nur Großbritannien schneller als das deutsche Mixed-Quartett. Dank der Team-Medaille schließt Gina Lückenkemper Frieden mit den Titelkämpfen in Birmingham.

spiegel.title: Waldbrände: Drei Tote bei Bränden auf griechischer Insel und in Spanien
spiegel.description: Starke Winde erschweren die Löscharbeiten: Auf der griechischen Insel Salamis und im nordostspanischen Aragon kämpfen Hunderte Einsatzkräfte gegen die Flammen. Für drei Menschen kam jedoch jede Hilfe zu spät.

spiegel.title: Russland: Diese Codes verwenden Soldaten, wenn sie vom Tod sprechen
spiegel.description: »Fleisch«, »Ankunft«, »Null«: Im Krieg gegen die Ukraine schreiben Soldaten Worten eine neue Bedeutung zu. Inzwischen nutzen auch Zivilisten den Militärjargon, um eine Realität zu beschreiben, die der Kreml negiert.

spiegel.title: Gaza-Friedensplan: US-Gesandter Jared Kushner berät mit Hamas-Spitze
spiegel.description: Trumps Schwiegersohn Jared Kushner wirbt in Ägypten für dessen Gaza-Friedensplan. Dazu führt er Gespräche mit Präsident el-Sisi und führenden Hamas-Vertretern. Die Hamas bekennt sich zu dem Plan – Israel lehnt ihn ab.

spiegel.title: Rheinland-Pfalz: Waldbrand im Westerwald – Evakuierung wieder beendet
spiegel.description: Im Westerwald dürfen die zuvor evakuierten Bewohnerinnen und Bewohner wieder in ihre Häuser und Wohnungen zurückkehren. Das Feuer brennt nun kontrolliert.

spiegel.title: Schwimm-EM in Paris: Isabel Gose nach drittem Silber im Becken nicht ganz zufrieden
spiegel.description: Nach Doppel-Gold im Freiwasser wollte Isabel Gose auch im Becken triumphieren. In drei Starts reichte es dreimal zu Silber, nicht aber zur vollkommenen Zufriedenheit.

spiegel.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Hochzeit mit Georgina im eigenen Wohnzimmer
spiegel.description: Wochenlang wurde über Ort und Termin spekuliert. Nun ist klar: Fußballstar Cristiano Ronaldo und Georgina Rodríguez haben sich im engsten Familienkreis das Jawort gegeben. Genau zehn Jahre nach ihrem ersten Treffen.

spiegel.title: Locarno Film Festival: An diesen Filmen zeigt sich, wie staatliche Willkür funktioniert
spiegel.description: Eben noch Staatsräson, jetzt unter Hochverratsverdacht: Beim Filmfestival von Locarno erinnern deutsche Filme und eine Retrospektive über Hollywoods Blacklist an die Unmöglichkeit zu wissen, in welcher Zeit man eigentlich lebt.

spiegel.title: Quantencomputer: Hochschule Karlsruhe plant Lehrrechner mit Diamant-Chip
spiegel.description: An der Hochschule Karlsruhe sollen Studierende am eigenen Quantencomputer lernen. Geld vom Land gibt es nicht. Also sammelt Studiendekan Philipp Nenninger Spenden – mit erstem Erfolg.

spiegel.title: K-Beauty: Hype um Kosmetik aus Südkorea – sind die Produkte ihr Geld wert?
spiegel.description: Der neue Hype um Seren, Cremes und Gesichtsmasken aus Südkorea erreicht auch deutsche Drogeriemärkte. Sind die Produkte ihren Preis wert?

spiegel.title: Großbrände: Lage in Nordrhein-Westfalen entspannt sich
spiegel.description: Nach den Großbränden in Hürtgenwald dürfen evakuierte Menschen in ihre Häuser zurückkehren, auch in Monschau kehrt etwas Ruhe ein. Die Behörden warnen jedoch vor starker Rauchbelastung.

spiegel.title: Ex-Bundestrainerin Martina Voss-Tecklenburg trainiert künftig FC Zürich
spiegel.description: Martina Voss-Tecklenburg hat nach ihrer Zeit beim DFB einen neuen Job gefunden. Für die frühere Bundestrainerin geht es zurück in die Schweiz, wo sie bereits zwischen 2012 und 2018 tätig war.

spiegel.title: Community Shield: Arsenal siegt, Kai Havertz vermiest Enzo Maresca das Debüt
spiegel.description: Der FC Arsenal feiert einen Traumstart in die neue Saison und führt im Community Shield gegen ManCity schon nach 23 Sekunden. Später legt Kai Havertz nach, Enzo Marescas Debüt als City-Trainer misslingt völlig.

letemps.description:
La mutation des rapports de force géopolitiques, l’intelligence artificielle et la dette publique croissante modifient de manière fondamentale le cadre des marchés des capitaux. letemps.description:
Seuls trois matchs des 32es de finale de la compétition ont donné lieu à un renversement hiérarchique. Aucune formation romande professionnelle n’a été surprise, même si Xamax a dû passer par une séance de tirs au but pour éliminer Meyrin

letemps.title: Chahutée par la critique, «L’Odyssée» de Christopher Nolan triomphe auprès des hellénistes romands
letemps.description:
Tandis que la très réputée traductrice britannique Emily Wilson étrille un film «grandiloquent et superficiel», des spécialistes suisses encensent une vision à la hauteur d’Homère. Plaidoyers homériques

letemps.title: «Apercevoir des bas en nylon fait battre mon cœur très fort»: la place des textures dans la sexualité

This statement by the astronomer Carl Sagan refers to the fact that elements heavier than hydrogen and helium were forged in the centers of the first stars. But how does this star-stuff evolve into the chemistry of rocks, plants and people?

phys-org.title: Brief firearm safety talks more than double openness to out-of-home storage
phys-org.description: A brief chat about firearm safety can sharply increase willingness among gun owners to consider temporarily storing their firearms outside the home during times of crisis, a step that could help reduce suicide risk, according to a Rutgers-led study.

phys-org.title: Hurricane Lala pulls away from Hawaii's Big Island
phys-org.description: Hurricane Lala was pulling away from Hawaii's Big Island early Sunday as heavy rain and strong winds struck the U.S. Pacific state and officials warned of potentially dangerous flooding.

phys-org.title: Belgium races to tame huge wildfire creeping toward Germany
phys-org.description: Water-bombing aircraft and farmers' tractors joined forces Sunday to help firefighters tame Belgium's largest modern-day wildfire, which has scorched vast swaths of a hard-to-reach nature reserve near the German border.

phys-org.title: Japan aims for the moons of Mars
phys-org.description: Japanese scientists are readying a mission to Mars' moons to retrieve samples that may unlock the origins of the solar system and life on Earth, although a rival Chinese mission aims to make it back first.

phys-org.title: A small squeeze reveals new clues about an unusual kind of magnet
phys-org.description: Researchers at Rice University have found that gently squeezing a crystal of iron sulfide can change two of its unusual properties at the same time: its tiny magnetic signal and the way electricity moves through it. The result gives scientists a clearer picture of how a newly recognized class of magnetic materials works and suggests a simple way to control their behavior.

phys-org.title: Gene-edited beagles produce no detectable major dog allergen, early tests find
phys-org.description: Humans love dogs, but petting them can leave some people sneezing and wheezing. About 15% of the world's population lives with a dog allergy, which can increase the risk of hay fever and asthma. The main culprit is Can f 1, a protein found mainly in dog saliva. Right now, staying away from furry friends or getting regular immunotherapy shots or tablets is the only way to deal with the symptoms.

phys-org.title: Phytophthora dieback linked to habitat loss and lower digging activity among quendas in Western Australia
phys-org.description: A new study from Murdoch University has found that the introduced plant disease Phytophthora dieback is indirectly hindering quendas in Western Australia's jarrah forests by reducing their habitat quality and consequently decreasing their digging activity. The paper, "Exotic Plant Pathogen Reduces Habitat and Foraging Activities of a Digging Mammal," was published in the journal Austral Ecology.

phys-org.title: Strain flips Hall signal in altermagnetic manganese telluride, suggesting a path to practical spintronics
phys-org.description: Time-reversal symmetry is an exotic behavior found in systems whose internal physics looks different when running forward versus backward in time. For some time, physicists have searched for this behavior in systems with almost no overall magnetization. Such phases are highly prized for spintronics, where information is carried using the quantum spins of electrons.

phys-org.title: Chinese ship sets off for Europe through Arctic, halving travel time
phys-org.description: A Chinese container vessel has set sail for Europe through the Arctic as part of a new weekly service on a route that cuts shipment times in half but that environmental groups warn could speed up the melting of polar ice.

phys-org.title: Firefighters battle second day of blaze on Greek island
phys-org.description: Firefighters battled for a second day Sunday to contain a forest fire on the Greek Aegean island of Skyros, as the local mayor voiced hope it could soon be brought under control.

phys-org.title: Shrinking water bodies can turn drought into disease hotspots or dead ends
phys-org.description: Prolonged dry spells or droughts can sometimes reduce aquatic diseases, many of which affect people. Yet other times, water scarcity can counterintuitively lead to an uptick in diseases that depend on water.

phys-org.title: Einstein Probe catches rare X-ray flash from an exploding star
phys-org.description: Astronomers have linked an X-ray flash discovered by the Einstein Probe to a known type of supernova with unusual features that point to the birth of an ultra-dense, rapidly spinning magnetar. The paper outlining this finding was published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters on July 22.

phys-org.title: Active particles could make stable glasses stronger without catastrophic brittle failure
phys-org.description: The strongest glasses have an Achilles' heel that causes them to fail catastrophically when pushed past their limit. They do not bend or stretch, as all damage concentrates into a single plane and the material fails in an instant. This brittleness has long capped the usefulness of high-stability amorphous solids, from bulk metallic glasses to engineered metamaterials.

phys-org.title: Why AI training can backfire for older workers
phys-org.description: Employers are increasingly investing in training to prepare their employees for artificial intelligence (AI). Training budgets are growing, and "upskilling" has become a common response to rapid technological change.

phys-org.title: Centuries-old physics test could help detect millicharged particles
phys-org.description: Theoretical physicists have long predicted the existence of millicharged particles (mCPs), hypothetical particles that carry a very small electric charge. These particles are expected to interact very weakly with ordinary matter and electromagnetic fields; hence, they would be difficult to detect in conventional particle physics experiments.

phys-org.title: Black hole star: Astronomers discover a brand-new type of astrophysical object
phys-org.description: Astronomers at MIT and elsewhere have spotted an extremely bright red spot in the early universe. The object resembles an enormous star, roughly the size of our solar system. But it also is putting out 100 billion times more energy than any known star can physically produce. In fact, such energies are closer to what a black hole might generate.

phys-org.title: Nature has spent billions of years fighting bacteria. AI could help us learn its secrets
phys-org.description: Tiny viruses that infect bacteria could one day help us tackle infections that antibiotics can no longer treat. But first, scientists need to understand how these viruses work, and artificial intelligence could provide them with a powerful way to do that.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: What Should Be Done About Asia’s Undervalued Currencies?
proj-syn.description: Those who worry that the renminbi, yen, and won are undervalued vis-à-vis the dollar are usually focused on the large trade and current-account surpluses that China, Japan, and Korea run with the US. But coordinated intervention in currency markets will not address the fundamentals underlying these imbalances.

proj-syn.title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
proj-syn.description: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe than many feared, corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity. To that end, governments should consider what policy incentives are in place, and large employers should consider their own long-term interests.

proj-syn.title: The Making and Remaking of Chinese Totalitarianism
proj-syn.description: For decades, the West assumed that economic growth would turn China into a more open, liberal society, much as it did South Korea and Taiwan. Instead, China’s totalitarian institutions proved remarkably resilient, surviving decades of reform and reasserting themselves under President Xi Jinping.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Not Forget Multilateral Institutions
proj-syn.description: The roadmap for middle-power action that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb recently laid out calls for countries that share interests to create ad hoc coalitions. But to be effective, these coalitions must work as much as possible within existing multilateral institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

crunchbase.description: Databricks is back raising another $5 billion, after it raised that amount just eight months ago. The largest fundings this week also went to an AI neolab, data center and electricity storage, defense, coding and biotech. Let’s take a look.

crunchbase.description: The sectors leading the herd to the Unicorn Board in July, by count, were financial services, robotics, AI orchestration, multimodal AI, energy and semiconductors, with the U.S. adding nearly half of the month's newly minted unicorns.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker

crunchbase.title: How A Teenage Carpenter Became The Founder Of AI Construction Startup Trunk Tools
crunchbase.description: Our second in a series of articles about non-tech founders getting venture funding features Sarah Buchner, a "blue-collar worker by background" who set out to find a way to help construction companies manage their projects more efficiently using AI agents.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: ClearJet raises $25M to build the ‘Uber of Cargo’
crunchbase.description: Austin-based ClearJet, an AI-enabled logistics technology startup connects shippers with unused cargo capacity on commercial flights, has raised a $25 million Edison Partners-led Series B, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Fitness Startup Funding Is Rebounding, But Investors Want AI And Data, Not Treadmills
crunchbase.description: Venture investors seem to be more upbeat than they have been in years about the future of fitness and wellness. Startup investment in those categories totaled more than $3.6 billion in the first half of this year, putting 2026 on pace to come in about a third higher than 2025.

crunchbase.title: The VC Firm That Helped Build Latin America’s Startup Scene Is Crossing Into Silicon Valley
crunchbase.description: Monashees, one of Latin America's oldest and most influential VC firms, believes the next phase of the region's startup ecosystem requires a permanent Silicon Valley presence, opening a San Francisco office last year. We spoke with firm partner Fabiola Quinzaños to talk through the firm's evolution and how it is meeting this AI moment.

crunchbase.title: AI-Native, Not AI-Sprinkle: Why AI Is A Business Change, Not A Technology Change
crunchbase.description: Companies unlock AI’s biggest productivity gains not by adding AI tools to existing workflows, but by redesigning teams, roles and daily work around AI. The broader lesson, argues Bob Morse, co-founder and managing partner of Strattam Capital, is that achieving transformational gains like 3x productivity requires CEO- and board-backed organizational change — not merely technology adoption.

crunchbase.title: Global New Unicorn Counts In The First Half Of 2026 Have Already Surpassed 2025’s Totals
crunchbase.description: A total 195 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in the first half of 2026 — far surpassing counts seen since the second half of 2022. Already, H1 is above the new unicorn totals for all of 2025, when 193 companies were minted with that status.

crunchbase.title: The Biggest Consequence Of An AI IPO Isn’t The IPO Itself. It’s What Happens Afterward.
crunchbase.description: A wave of major AI IPOs could return significant liquidity to limited partners, fueling a new venture fundraising cycle rather than simply affecting public-market valuations. That capital is likely to flow disproportionately to the largest, established VC firms, writes guest author Andrew Gershfeld of Flint Capital, creating a concentration flywheel that could reshape fundraising, startup financing and power across the venture ecosystem.
